subject: pharmacology
title: Proton Pump Inhibitors, H2 Blockers, and Mucosal Protective Agents in Acid Peptic Disease

steps.tx: The prototypical substituted benzimidazole prodrug that functions as an irreversible gastric proton pump inhibitor is **omeprazole**. Formulated as enteric-coated granules to survive acidic gastric transit, omeprazole is absorbed in the alkaline proximal small intestine and distributes via circulation into the acidic canaliculi of parietal cells. There, protonation traps the molecule and catalyzes its conversion into active sulfenamide and sulfenic acid, which covalently form disulfide bonds with cysteine residues of the luminal H+/K+ ATPase, permanently inactivating the pump until new enzyme molecules are synthesized.
steps.say: Omeprazole accumulates in acidic parietal canaliculi, converting into active sulfenamide to permanently inactivate proton pumps.

nodes.label: Enteric-coated omeprazole absorbed in proximal small intestine
Concentrates in acidic parietal canaliculi (pH < 1.0) via ion trapping
Acid-catalyzed rearrangement to active cationic sulfenamide
Covalent disulfide bonding with Cys813 on luminal H+/K+ ATPase

steps.tx: A chemically stable substituted benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor distinguished by lower affinity for hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes is **pantoprazole**. Available in both oral and intravenous formulations, pantoprazole selectively binds to cysteine-813 and cysteine-822 on the gastric H+/K+ ATPase enzyme. Because pantoprazole undergoes hepatic clearance predominantly via sulfotransferase conjugation and only weakly inhibits CYP2C19, it does not impede the bioactivation of clopidogrel, making it the preferred intravenous and oral proton pump inhibitor in acute coronary syndromes and dual antiplatelet therapy.
steps.say: Pantoprazole is cleared by sulfotransferases with minimal CYP2C19 inhibition, making it safe alongside clopidogrel.

left.title: Pantoprazole (Favorable CYP Profile)
points: Chemically stable benzimidazole; oral and intravenous routes
Cleared predominantly via cytosolic sulfotransferase conjugation
Minimal inhibition of hepatic CYP2C19 or CYP3A4 isozymes
Safe to co-administer with antiplatelet prodrug clopidogrel

right.title: Omeprazole (CYP2C19 Inhibitor)
points: Prototypical oral benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor

steps.tx: The most potent pharmacological suppressors of gastric hydrochloric acid secretion available in clinical practice are **proton pump inhibitors** (PPIs). By targeting the final common pathway of acid production, the luminal H+/K+ ATPase exchanger, PPIs inhibit both basal and meal-stimulated acid secretion by greater than ninety percent, regardless of whether stimulation originates from gastrin, histamine, or acetylcholine. In contrast to H2 blockers, PPIs maintain intragastric pH above 4 for fourteen to sixteen hours daily, providing superior healing of peptic ulcers and reflux esophagitis.
steps.say: Proton pump inhibitors target the final common H+/K+ ATPase pathway to suppress acid secretion by over ninety percent.

steps.tx: A competitive, reversible antagonist of histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells developed as a second-generation agent is **ranitidine**. Structurally incorporating a furan ring that avoids the antiandrogenic gynecomastia and extensive CYP450 enzyme inhibition characteristic of cimetidine, ranitidine suppresses basal and nocturnal gastric acid secretion by seventy percent. While historically a cornerstone of peptic ulcer and GERD therapy, commercial ranitidine formulations were withdrawn globally due to contamination with the probable human carcinogen N-nitrosodimethylamine.
steps.say: Ranitidine was a second-generation H2 blocker withdrawn worldwide due to nitrosodimethylamine contamination.

rows: Negligible inhibition; withdrawn for NDMA impurity
Zero inhibition of hepatic CYP450 enzymes

steps.tx: The most potent thiazole-containing competitive histamine H2 receptor antagonist currently utilized in clinical practice is **famotidine**. Demonstrating twenty-to-fifty times greater acid-inhibitory potency than cimetidine, famotidine suppresses basal, nocturnal, and pentagastrin-stimulated gastric acid output for ten to twelve hours without inhibiting hepatic CYP450 isozymes or displaying antiandrogenic activity. It is widely indicated for mild gastroesophageal reflux disease, duodenal ulcer healing, and prevention of stress ulcers in critically ill intensive care patients.
steps.say: Famotidine is a potent thiazole H2 antagonist providing ten to twelve hours of nocturnal acid suppression without drug interactions.

left.title: Famotidine (H2 Receptor Antagonist)
points: Reversibly blocks basolateral parietal H2 receptors

Rapid onset of action; ideal for episodic on-demand heartburn

steps.tx: A basic aluminum hydroxide complex of sulfated sucrose that serves as a non-absorbable mucosal protective cytoprotective agent is **sucralfate**. In an acidic gastric environment with a pH below 4.0, sucralfate undergoes extensive cross-linking and polymerization into a viscous, sticky paste that adheres selectively to positively charged proteins exposed in the crater base of peptic ulcers. This physical barrier resists acid, pepsin, and bile salt penetration for six hours while stimulating local prostaglandin and epidermal growth factor synthesis. It requires acidic pH and must not be taken with antacids or PPIs.
steps.say: Sucralfate polymerizes in acidic environments to coat ulcer craters, requiring separation from antacids and PPIs.

nodes.label: Oral administration of sucralfate suspension on an empty stomach
Acid-catalyzed (pH < 4.0) polymerization into viscous polyanionic paste

steps.tx: An insoluble heavy metal salt formulation that exerts multi-factorial topical antimicrobial and gastroprotective actions is **bismuth**. In the stomach, bismuth complexes with mucosal glycoproteins to coat ulcer bases, inhibits pepsin proteolytic activity, and stimulates endogenous mucosal prostaglandin and bicarbonate release. Crucially, bismuth exerts direct bactericidal action against Helicobacter pylori by disrupting bacterial cell wall synthesis and inhibiting urease and catalase enzymes, serving as an indispensable anchor of quadruple eradication regimens.
steps.say: Bismuth salts coat ulcer bases and exert direct bactericidal activity against Helicobacter pylori in quadruple therapy.

steps.tx: While proton pump inhibitors exhibit an exceptional safety profile during acute and short-term courses, prolonged multi-year administration carries **chronic PPI safety hazards**. Long-term profound achlorhydria impairs the gastric absorption of vitamin B12, non-heme iron, and calcium, predisposing elderly patients to osteoporosis, vertebral fractures, and hip fractures. Furthermore, loss of the protective gastric acid barrier permits colonization of the gastrointestinal tract by pathogens, significantly increasing the clinical incidence of Clostridioides difficile colitis, bacterial gastroenteritis, and hospital-acquired pneumonia.
steps.say: Chronic proton pump inhibitor therapy impairs calcium and iron absorption, predisposing to hip fractures and Clostridioides difficile.
